articles.headline: Bijan Robinson: Falcons deserved boos in loss to Chiefs
articles.description: Fans at Mercedes-Benz Stadium booed the Falcons after another poor offensive showing Sunday.
articles.headlineJa: ビジャン・ロビンソン：チーフスに敗れたファルコンズにブーイングは妥当だった
articles.descriptionJa: 日曜日の試合で再び攻撃陣が低調なパフォーマンスを見せ、メルセデス・ベンツ・スタジアムのファンからファルコンズにブーイングが飛んだ。
articles.body:
ATLANTA -- The Falcons' offense was stagnant at best for a third straight week during a 35-13 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday.

And the fans at Mercedes-Benz Stadium let the team know about it, showering the offense with boos after some failed third downs.

The Falcons started the game with four straight three-and-outs, the first time that's happened to them since 2000.

"They put in their hard-earned work every single week to try to make it to these games, and it's our job to make it count for them," Falcons star running back Bijan Robinson said of the fans. "So yeah, when they boo us, we deserve it."

It was the most boos the Falcons have received since Week 2, when they were routed by the Carolina Panthers.

Then between Weeks 3 and 7, the Falcons scored a league-high 31 points per game. But over the last three weeks -- losses to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Cincinnati Bengals and now the Chiefs -- Atlanta has scored a combined total of 30 points.

The Falcons (3-7) did make an adjustment entering this game. Offensive coordinator and playcaller Tommy Rees moved down to the sideline from the coaches' box. But it didn't make a huge difference.

Atlanta was 5-of-16 on third downs and 1-for-5 in the red zone. Quarterback Michael Penix Jr. was 23-of-43 for 286 yards with an interception. Robinson had 71 yards on just 16 carries.

Robinson has not had 20 or more carries since the team's Week 7 win over the San Francisco 49ers. The Falcons have lost five of their last six games, and Robinson did not hit the 20-carry mark in any of those losses.

"The responsibility falls on me," Atlanta coach Kevin Stefanski said. "All of this falls on me. So I'll take responsibility for everything that goes on in this football team. We all have to be better. That's the truth. We will all learn from it, not going to hide from it, going to own it and then make corrections."

Despite the recent skid, the Falcons (3-7) are just two games in the loss column behind the first-place Panthers (4-5). The NFC South remains wide open, and Atlanta, which has its bye next week, will play three division foes in consecutive games to finish the season.

"We're not out yet," Penix said. "We just got to win ... We've gotta win each and every week. We've got seven games left and we got to win."

articles.headline: Raiders lose TE Brock Bowers to ankle injury vs. Seahawks
articles.description: Brock Bowers was ruled out of Sunday's matchup against the Seahawks after suffering a right ankle injury in the opening quarter.
articles.headlineJa: レイダース、シーホークス戦でTEブロック・バワーズが足首の負傷で離脱
articles.descriptionJa: ブロック・バワーズは第1クォーターに右足首を負傷し、日曜日のシーホークス戦への出場が見送られた。
articles.body:
LAS VEGAS -- Raiders tight end Brock Bowers was ruled out of Sunday's matchup against the Seattle Seahawks after suffering a right ankle injury in the opening quarter.

Bowers was hurt during the Raiders' opening drive. He remained on the ground after Ashton Jeanty's rushing attempt before walking off the field under his own power. Bowers went into the medical tent and then returned to the field for Fernando Mendoza's 10-yard touchdown run.

Bowers then headed to the locker room after that play and was listed as questionable to return by the team.

However, he returned with 13:30 to go in the second quarter and made a 12-yard reception on third down. Later in the quarter, Bowers went back into the locker room, where he stayed for the rest of the first half before ultimately being ruled out.

When healthy, Bowers has been one of the league's best pass catchers this season. He entered Week 10 with 48 catches for 658 yards and six touchdowns and recorded at least 70 receiving yards in seven straight games.

But he has also battled injury issues and underwent a knee procedure in September that caused him to miss the Raiders' first two games this season.

articles.headline: LeBron James dishes 11 assists in 76ers win, passing Kidd for third in NBA ranks
articles.description: LeBron James moved past Hall of Fame point guard Jason Kidd for third on the NBA's career assists list with 12,092.
articles.headlineJa: レブロン・ジェームズ、76ersの勝利に貢献し11アシストを記録、キッドを抜きNBA歴代3位へ
articles.descriptionJa: レブロン・ジェームズは通算12,092アシストを記録し、殿堂入りのポイントガード、ジェイソン・キッドを抜いてNBA歴代アシストランキング3位に浮上した。
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- As LeBron James leaped for a contested layup over the outstretched arms of Indiana Pacers forward Pascal Siakam and guard Aaron Nesmith on Sunday, James turned and passed the ball to Sixers guard Tyrese Maxey for a 3-pointer.

It was a pass that only James knew was coming, and it was one of eleven assists in Sunday's 131-124 win over Indiana that moved him past Hall of Fame point guard Jason Kidd for third on the NBA career assists list with 12,092.

"It's super humbling. It's something that I didn't obviously foresee in my career," James said. "But I knew assists meant a lot to me. Just the movement of the ball, being able to find my teammates and put the ball on time and on target."

James finished Sunday's game with 15 points, 11 assists and seven rebounds. The eleventh assist, which pushed James past Kidd, came in the fourth quarter on a pass to guard VJ Edgecombe. James has thrived as a passer against the Pacers this year, posting his top two assist totals of the season against them -- including 10 against Indiana on Oct. 28.

 

Throughout the night, James had a handful of highlight-worthy dimes. There was a no-look pass to a cutting Jaylen Brown that drew roars from the crowd at Xfinity Mobile Arena, as well as the pass to Maxey. James said that his new teammates adjusted to his passes by necessity, after James "hit them in the head a couple times," with passes throughout training camp.

"You can ask VJ [Edgecombe] for sure. I hit VJ a couple times," James said with a smile.

But he and Maxey have trained together in the offseason for the last six years, so they have a different level of chemistry, James said. But even Maxey wasn't sure that the pass in the first quarter was coming. He stood ready in shooting position but then dropped his hands as James rose before quickly adjusting as the ball headed toward him.

"I knew once I got his defender to stare at me, I was going to 'Rese," James said. "It caught 'Rese by surprise. He was like, 'Yo, I didn't even believe that you was gonna pass the ball.' So you know, I just tell my guys, I mean, 'Always just pay attention to me when I got the ball because I definitely see plays develop before they happen.'"

A few minutes before that play, Maxey and James had a failed connection. On the opening possession of the game, James threw a bounce pass to a cutting Maxey, who missed the layup.

"I missed at the rim because ... I was just jogging through and I was not playing to get the ball," Maxey said. "And the ball hit me in my chest, and I looked up; I was at the rim, so I laid in, and I missed it. But it's just like plays like that where you need to be ready at all times."

James could continue to climb the charts this season, as he is 461 assists away from passing point guard Chris Paul for second all time. The top spot, held by former Utah Jazz point guard John Stockton, is a ways away at 15,062 assists.

For the season, James is averaging 15.1 points, 7.2 rebounds and 6.9 assists

articles.descriptionJa: 来夏に契約が切れるため、ブルーノ・フェルナンデスのマンチェスター・ユナイテッドでの将来は不透明であると報じられている。Transfer Talkが最新情報を伝える。
articles.body:
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes is holding off on signing a new contract for now, while Arsenal are the latest team to join a long list of admirers following Middlesbrough striker Will Lankshear. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes is holding off on signing a new contract for now, says The Sun. Fernandes, 32, has a contract which expires next summer -- albeit with a one-year club option to renew -- and reportedly wants to wait to see what happens under new boss Mauricio Pochettino. The Portugal midfielder has been linked with a lucrative move to Saudi Arabia before.

- Arsenal are in the market for a center forward, and TEAMtalk claims that the Gunners are the latest team to join a long list of admirers following Middlesbrough striker Will Lankshear. The 21-year-old joined Boro from Tottenham Hotspur this summer, after a loan spell at Oxford United in the Championship, and has hit the ground running, scoring 13 goals in as many appearances in the league so far. That has brought about plenty of transfer interest, but Middlesbrough will try to block any exit in January.

- Arsenal are continuing the push to sign a left-sided forward, with RB Leipzig star Antonio Nusa leading their shortlist, says TEAMtalk. Gabriel Martinelli and Leandro Trossard left in the summer, and were replaced by Christos Tzolis before a move to sign Vinícius Júnior from Real Madrid fell short. With Mikel Arteta wanting more options on that flank, the report claims that talks have opened with Nusa's representatives about a possible switch, but the 21-year-old's transfer could cost €80 million.

- Tottenham defender Pedro Porro has decided that he only wants to join Barcelona if he leaves the club, according to Sport. The 27-year-old Spain right back has seen interest from the Blaugrana, as well as Real Madrid, despite only signing a new contract with Spurs in the summer. But while Barcelona are eyeing up a deal worth no more than €50 million next summer, Tottenham will stand firm on their €70 million valuation.

- AC Milan are looking to bolster in the forward areas during January, with Gazzetta dello Sport reporting that Real Madrid's Endrick and Club Brugge's Nicolò Tresoldi are on their shortlist. Endrick has seen few minutes in the starting XI for Los Blancos this season and Milan are keen on a loan deal with a permanent option included. Meanwhile, Tresoldi  22, who has five goals in four Champions League appearances this season, has caught the eye of a number of a teams and could move in a €60 million deal.

articles.headline: Inside the Jordan Dome, where 'Space Jam' pickup games helped MJ get his game back
articles.description: Thirty years after "Space Jam," those who shared the summer with Jordan remember the basketball that unfolded offscreen.
articles.headlineJa: ジョーダン・ドーム内部へ：『スペース・ジャム』のピックアップゲームがMJの調子を取り戻させた場所
articles.descriptionJa: 『スペース・ジャム』から30年。ジョーダンと共にあの夏を過ごした人々が、スクリーン外で繰り広げられたバスケットボールを回想する。
articles.body:
Michael Jordan had seen enough.

With rising UCLA sophomore and national champion Kris Johnson defending him, reigning NBA All-Star Cedric Ceballos wouldn't let the youngster go away easily. Ceballos had been "busting my ass," Johnson told ESPN, and talking smack while doing it.

At North Carolina, a poster of five-time NBA All-Star Marques, Kris' father, hung in Jordan's dorm room. Jordan had recently taken Johnson under his wing. So with Ceballos picking on Johnson, Jordan took action. He would guard Ceballos and Kris switched onto another All-Star, Reggie Miller.

"I'm like, 'OK, all right, what's going on over here?' And then Mike just systematically just went to attack Ceballos on multiple possessions," Johnson told ESPN.

In Johnson's words, Jordan "dismantled" Ceballos with multiple buckets in a row and delivered the trash talk back. Rocking the patent leather Jordan 11s, he jab faked with the ball palmed looking down and expressing his disdain that Ceballos wore 23 in the league -- Jordan's jersey number.

Johnson and Jordan won the game, a pickup held on the Warner Bros. lot in the summer of 1995 while Jordan filmed "Space Jam." The intensity of those runs rivaled a playoff atmosphere, and that interaction with Ceballos showed Johnson something.

"My takeaway, wow, Mike's a crazy motherf---er. He's really in real life, he's really that dude," Johnson said.

Jordan had just returned to the NBA after leaving to play baseball. The Orlando Magic defeated him and the Bulls in the playoffs, celebrating emphatically on the Bulls' home court.

It marked the first time since 1990 that Jordan's Bulls didn't play in the NBA Finals. For all intents and purposes, it wouldn't be a normal offseason. Add in a potential distraction with "Space Jam" responsibilities, and Chicago's three-peat could've been one-and-done.  But, this was Michael Jordan. He had Warner Bros. build the "Jordan Dome" on the lot. The six-week schedule included shooting scenes with "Monstars" by day, and hooping against the NBA's own "Monstars" by night: Reggie Miller, Patrick Ewing, Grant Hill, Charles Barkley, Shaquille O'Neal, Alonzo Mourning and more.

Sunday marks the 30th anniversary of "Space Jam," which grossed $250.2 million worldwide against an $80 million budget to become the highest-grossing basketball film at the time. Jordan Brand commemorated the anniversary with a new six-part documentary that began Sunday. While the basketball on camera with the Looney Tunes drove that box-office success, the basketball played off camera helped shape Jordan's next act.

The pickup games at the Jordan Dome helped prepare him for Chicago's 72-10 season and another three-peat, gave fellow players a confidence boost and, according to his longtime trainer Tim Grover, served as an informal tryout for his future Bulls teammate.

articles.headline: Reaction as Brazil legend Ronaldinho comes out of retirement at Ravenna
articles.description: Ronaldinho came out of retirement to play for Italian Serie C side Ravenna at age 46 in a bid to score his 300th career goal, but couldn't manage it. Here's what happened.
articles.headlineJa: ブラジルの伝説ロナウジーニョがラヴェンナで現役復帰、周囲の反応は？
articles.descriptionJa: ロナウジーニョはキャリア300ゴール目を達成するため、46歳でイタリア・セリエCのラヴェンナに加入し現役復帰したが、目標達成には至らなかった。その詳細をレポートする。
articles.body:
Former Barcelona and AC Milan forward Ronaldinho, 46, came out of retirement on Sunday to play for Italian Serie C club Ravenna against Forli, but could only play for 45 minutes.

The Brazil legend retired on 299 career goals, with his final match for Fluminense in September 2015, and he chose a third-tier club in Italy to try and reach the magic number of 300. However, despite a few neat flicks and tricks, he was unable to get on the scoresheet.

The 2002-World Cup champion and back-to-back FIFA World Player of the Year nearly got an assist when his corner found the head of Giulio Donati, but was well saved. And he played a small part in the opening goal as he held off an opponent before the ball found its way to Donati who unleashed a shot that former Brazil defender Roberto Carlos would have been proud of.

Catch up on everything that happened.

articles.headline: USMNT's Balogun does 'Dame Time' celebration after goal vs. Haiti
articles.description: After the star forward found the back of the net against Haiti, he had a specific celebration in mind: Damian Lillard's iconic "Dame Time" motion.
articles.body:
It was Dame Time for USMNT striker Folarin Balogun on Saturday.

The U.S. attack rolled against Haiti in the first leg of the two nations' Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal tie, producing six goals for a 6-0 rout. The last of that scoring barrage came off the foot of Balogun, who entered the game off the bench in the 66th minute before scoring in the 82nd.

And after the star forward found the back of the net, he had a very specific celebration in mind: Portland Trail Blazers guard Damian Lillard's iconic "Dame Time" motion. Balogun pointed to his wrist repeatedly as he ran toward a gaggle of USMNT substitutes in celebration.

Following the game, Balogun took to X to further underscore his tribute, posting a clip of the celebration and a photo of Lillard doing the motion.

It wasn't the only time Balogun brought out the celebration on Saturday afternoon -- the forward had also done the motion after a 75th-minute goal, but that tally was disallowed after a VAR review.

It's also not the first time Balogun has turned to memorable NBA celebrations for inspiration after scoring. After he opened the scoring for the U.S. against Bosnia and Herzegovina in the World Cup round of 32, Balogun did LeBron James' "silencer" motion. Coincidentally, that celebration also became official on the second attempt -- he had done it on a prior disallowed goal in that game, too.

articles.headline: Sunday's fantasy basketball adds and bets to make in the NBA
articles.description: Jim McCormick breaks down Sunday's slate, highlighting the fantasy streamers to add and bets to make.
articles.body:
A busy nine-game Sunday slate tips off this afternoon in South Philly with a matinee matchup between the Philadelphia 76ers and Indiana Pacers. With just a third of today's games featuring double-digit spreads, Sunday shapes up as a potentially competitive and compelling day of basketball.

Even though it's just mid-November, injuries are influencing nearly every rotation and matchup around the league. Key scorers absent from today's slate include Joel Embiid, Tyrese Haliburton, Austin Reaves, Brandon Ingram, Jaren Jackson Jr., Kon Knueppel, Kawhi Leonard, Lauri Markkanen, Jusuf Nurkic, Chet Holmgren, and Fred VanVleet.

Today's action should reveal more about how teams are adjusting, which players are taking on expanded responsibilities, and where opportunities emerge deeper in rotations. These situations can also uncover developing roles and skills that might otherwise remain hidden when teams are at full strength.

When it comes to predicting which games could offer the most offensive upside, point totals can serve as a useful guide. Today's contest between the New York Knicks and Toronto Raptors has a projected total of just 217.5 points, suggesting that a lower-scoring grind will unfold. Meanwhile, in Milwaukee, the Bucks host the Atlanta Hawks in a game with a total of 234.5 -- the highest of the day and an indicator of a fun scoring climate.

Lower projected totals do not eliminate the possibility of strong individual statistical performances. That said, slate-changing fantasy production is more likely to come from games with favorable offensive environments, where the potential for points and overall production is greater.

With an eye toward uncovering compelling betting angles and fantasy decisions, let's take a look at the day ahead in the NBA.

Fantasy stream team 

Players available in at least 50% of ESPN leagues who you should you pick up for today.

Brook Lopez, C, LA Clippers (rostered in 28.3% of leagues)

Enjoying a revival as a high-volume perimeter scorer, Lopez has somehow produced at least 20 points in three of his last four games. A matchup with a Sacramento Kings team that sits 26th in rebounding percentage likely means added possessions for Lopez and his peers. Add in the potential for multiple blocks and you can see why "BroLo" leads today's selections.

Sandro Mamukelashvili, C, Los Angeles Lakers (11.6%)

The absence of Reaves opens up more shots for "Mamu," who has tallied 56 points across his last two games in this elevated role. The Phoenix Suns are smaller in the frontcourt than most opponents, setting up Mamukelashvili with double-double upside in this divisional matchup.

Kelly Oubre Jr., SF/SG, Pacers (7.4%)

Thriving as a chaos creator for the Pacers in recent games, Oubre is in a good spot to produce a fun line today. The Pacers have a long injury report, including questionable tags for Andrew Nembhard and Aaron Nesmith, supporting the idea Oubre will be busy against his former team today.

articles.headline: Haaland 'incredibly happy' at Man City, not thinking about possible sanctions
articles.description: Erling Haaland says he is "incredibly happy" at Manchester City and his focus is on performing and not on the potential sanctions against the club.
articles.body:
Erling Haaland says he is "incredibly happy" at Manchester City and his focus is on performing and not on the potential sanctions against the club.

City have appealed after being found guilty of more than 100 breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations.

The club could face heavy sanctions, including huge points deductions or demotion, should the verdict be upheld.

Haaland was asked about the case after Norway's 3-1 Nations League victory over Wales in Oslo on Saturday night, in which he scored his 66th goal in 60 international appearances.

"This is a question I struggle to answer, because it's a legal battle between the Premier League and Manchester City," Haaland told Norwegian broadcaster TV2.

"Am I supposed to answer that? I don't really know. It's a difficult question to answer when I don't know that much about it.

"To be completely honest, I'm focused on trying to perform for Manchester City. A club I signed a five-year deal with in 2022, and a new nine-and-a-half-year deal in late 2024.

"I think that says everything about the matter. I'm a City player and I'm incredibly happy there."

Asked if the situation affects his City future, Haaland replied: "I understand that you want a little headline here, but as I said I signed a long-term contract in 2024.

"I'd say I made a pretty good choice by joining City in 2022. We can all agree on that.

"I won't say it myself, but look at the trophies I've won and how I've developed on and off the pitch.

"I'm standing here after winning an international 3-1. Things aren't going so well in the Premier League, but we'll try to turn that around against Fulham [on Saturday]."

- MrBeast, meet Haaland: Man City star puts YouTuber through soccer gauntlet

- Man City charges outcome cannot leave 'room for doubt' - sports integrity chief

City maintain they have a "comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence" to support their case, despite being found guilty by an independent commission in September.

The commission's damning findings included breaches relating to the concealment of funding worth more than £830million over a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018.

Haaland said the period under investigation happened before he joined City, and in the interview he painstakingly pointed out each stage of his football journey during that time.

He also name checked fellow Norwegian players Abdisalam Ibrahim, Martin Samuelsen, Omar Elabdellaoui and Kjetil Haug, who spent time at City during that era.

Haaland said: "The investigation covered 2009-2018. I assume the answers will come.

"I don't know when. I haven't read much about it."

articles.headline: Arsenal's Bruno Guimarães: Learning a lot from 'machine' Declan Rice
articles.description: Bruno Guimarães has labelled Arsenal teammate Declan Rice a "machine" and said he's been learning a lot by playing alongside him.
articles.body:
Bruno Guimarães has labelled Arsenal teammate Declan Rice a "machine" and said he has been learning a lot by playing alongside him. 

The Brazil international joined Arsenal in the summer from Newcastle for £75 million ($101 million) and has made an impressive start to his career in north London. He has made 14 appearances in all competitions and scored two crucial goals in the Premier League against Sunderland and Leeds United. 

Guimarães has already shown signs of striking a good parternship with Rice in the middle of the park, and said their relationship extends beyond the field. 

"Look, I think that ever since he announced I was coming here, everything was practically set. He sent me a message right away saying: 'We've had a lot of fights in the past, but now we're friends -- we're going to play together. I'm really happy you're coming here. You're going to really raise the level of our team,'" he told ESPN Brazil. 

"So he was a guy who had already won me over even before I arrived. We know -- I'd say he's a complete player; he's a machine on the field. He can run, I don't know, 22 kilometers in a game without stopping for a second. I was really happy.

"I'm learning from him -- learning a lot from him -- since he's a very technical player. So, I think we have one of the best midfields in Europe here, yes -- given the number of players we have -- and anyway, I think Declan is a guy who's been helping me a lot; I felt right at home."

Guimarães joined Arsenal after five years at Newcastle, where he was the captain and beloved by the fanbase. He led the club to the 2025 Carabao Cup, their first domestic trophy in 70 years, and wrote himself into Newcastle's history books. 

So, leaving St. James' Park was "a very difficult decision" for him this summer. 

"I think I was one of the most beloved players during my time there, so it was a difficult decision, but in my mind, deep down, I felt I needed a new challenge. After almost five years at Newcastle, I think I'm driven by challenges and wanted a new one," he said.

- 'Extremely lucky' Declan Rice hints new Arsenal contract will be signed soon

- Max Dowman breaks Jude Bellingham's England record as youngest U21 player

"But, to be completely honest, it wasn't an easy decision. I had to think long and hard about it at the time. It was very difficult, too. Right after the World Cup, which was a very turbulent time -- so it was difficult for me in many ways. But in the end, I chose to make the move. I'm happy here; I'm starting my journey here as well.

"I think I'm increasingly understanding Arteta's approach -- which is completely different from what I was used to doing at Newcastle -- and I'm adapting more and more, getting to know the new players better. As I said, it's not easy to switch clubs after nearly five years, when you were already completely used to the routine, to everything. But I think this is a huge challenge, and I'm ready for it."

Information from ESPN Brazil's Artur Rocha,

articles.headline: Mauricio Pochettino to Man United: Is Tottenham love affair finally over?
articles.description: Mauricio Pochettino is back in the Premier League as the new Man United boss. For Tottenham fans, it's complicated.
articles.headlineJa: マウリシオ・ポチェッティーノがマンUへ：トッテナムとの愛の物語はついに終わるのか？
articles.descriptionJa: マウリシオ・ポチェッティーノがマンチェスター・ユナイテッドの新監督としてプレミアリーグに復帰します。トッテナムのファンにとっては、複雑な心境となるでしょう。
articles.body:
"He's magic, you know, Mauricio Pochettino!" For five years, these were the words that rang out amongst Tottenham fans.

First, at the old White Hart Lane -- a much-loved, if dilapidated, ground that became a fortress during Pochettino's years as head coach of the club. Then, at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium -- a magnificent arena that, in recent years, has felt more like a house of horrors than any sort of stronghold.

But now Pochettino is back in the Premier League, this time as Manchester United manager. And for Tottenham fans who once dreamed of seeing the Argentine return to north London, it's another reminder that the man who gave us so many unforgettable memories might never be coming home.

The Pochettino love affair

The Argentine manager joined Tottenham in 2014 and was at the helm of one of the best, and most beloved, Spurs teams in the club's history. Under Pochettino, Harry Kane (now a Ballon d'Or winner!), Son Heung-Min, Christian Eriksen, Dele Alli, Jan Vertonghen, Toby Alderweireld, Mousa Dembélé and Hugo Lloris all shone in ways that few football fans and pundits expected.

During the Pochettino era, Tottenham came agonisingly close to winning the Premier League and reached the Champions League final. They went an entire season unbeaten at home -- somewhat unthinkable now given the team's struggles at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium -- and played some of the most thrilling football in the league at the time.

There were famous victories over arch-rivals Arsenal and in Europe, including over Real Madrid and Borussia Dortmund, and, of course, there was that night in Amsterdam. When Lucas Moura scored an astonishing hat trick against Ajax to send Spurs to the Champions League final for the first time in our history.

For many Spurs fans, including myself, the Poch years brought some of our best ever memories of supporting the club. There was a special connection between Pochettino and fans. He was revered and many of us hoped that it would last forever -- even if we all knew that, really, nothing ever lasts that long. Especially not in football.

When Pochettino was sacked, rather unceremoniously, in November 2019 -- just months after taking us to the Champions League final -- it felt somewhat unjust.

It was clear for anyone to see in 2019 that Tottenham's squad was beginning to get stale in a number of areas and that what the club truly needed was a rebuild. For myriad reasons, that never came to fruition and so, when, results on the pitch took a nosedive in the winter of that year the axe fell on Pochettino.

Overnight, the man who had turned Tottenham into a truly formidable side capable of beating anyone on their day was gone. Since then, it's fair to say that no other manager that has taken the wheel at the club has managed to form the same sort of bond that Pochettino had with us.

Many have come and gone but it hasn't yet felt like any of them have "got" us the way that Pochettino did. It is early days under Roberto De Zerbi

articles.headline: Every Manchester United player, manager, executive since Glazers' takeover: Where are they now?
articles.description: The Glazer family took over Manchester United in 2005, but what has happened to the players, managers and executive staff since?
articles.body:
Manchester United have shuffled from one crisis to another since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013 after winning his 13th Premier League title.

The club were taken over in 2005 by American billionaires the Glazer family, but things have steadily unraveled under their leadership over the past 21 years and this season United have had their worst start to a Premier League season -- they sit just one point off the bottom of the table, having won once in 10 league games.

The finger of blame for United's woes has been pointed in many directions over the past decade or so, with the current hierarchy -- led by co-chairman Joel Glazer, minority owner Jim Ratcliffe, CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox -- taking plenty of flak for the recent malaise.

But a lot of different backroom senior staff have been involved in the club since 2005, a lot of different managers have tried and failed, and a lot of players have come and gone. So where are they now?

Jump to: Backroom staff | Managers | Incoming players

Backroom staff

David Gill (CEO)

Gill left his role in the summer of 2013 and worked as vice president of UEFA and FIFA, as well as serving as a vice-chairman of the English Football Association. Still a Man United board member, Gill stepped down from his role on the UEFA executive committee in 2025 and was named the chair at Telix Pharmaceuticals in September 2026.

Ed Woodward (executive vice-chairman)

Having advised the Glazer family during the takeover of Manchester United, Woodward was hired in 2005 and given charge of the commercial and media operations two years later. He replaced Gill as CEO in 2013 and left the club in February 2022.

Now, he is the co-owner of the Quinta da Pedra Alta vineyard in Portugal. He is also a partner at AGILIS Sports Advisory Group -- a London-based mergers and acquisitions boutique focused on the sports sector -- a trustee at the Bloomsbury Football Foundation, and a non-exec board member at Sentient Sports, which describes itself as "pioneering AI-driven athlete protection and sports innovation."

Matt Judge (director of football negotiations)

The former investment banker joined the club in 2012 and was involved in United's transfer business from 2014. He led contract negotiations under Woodward from 2016, but he took up a new role in March 2021 when Darren Fletcher was named technical director and John Murtough was promoted to football director before leaving in 2022. He is now a partner, alongside Woodward, at the aforementioned AGILIS Sports Advisory Group.

Dan Ashworth (sporting director)

Ashworth was named the FA's director of elite development in 2012. He moved to Brighton to become the club's technical director in 2019, before joining Newcastle United as sporting director in 2022. articles.headline: Portland faces Minnesota on 3-game win streak
articles.description: Portland Trail Blazers (9-3, fourth in the Western Conference) vs. Minnesota Timberwolves (9-4, fifth in the Western Conference)
articles.body:
Portland Trail Blazers (9-3, fourth in the Western Conference) vs. Minnesota Timberwolves (9-4, fifth in the Western Conference)


              Minneapolis; Monday, 8 p.m. EST


              BOTTOM LINE: Portland will attempt to build upon its three-game win streak with a victory over Minnesota.


              The Timberwolves are 5-2 against Western Conference opponents. Minnesota is the Western Conference leader with 13.8 offensive rebounds per game led by Rudy Gobert averaging 3.8.


              The Trail Blazers are 9-3 against Western Conference opponents. Portland averages 119.6 points and has outscored opponents by 7.8 points per game.


              The 118.3 points per game the Timberwolves score are 6.5 more points than the Trail Blazers give up (111.8). The Trail Blazers are shooting 46.9% from the field, 3.5% higher than the 43.4% the Timberwolves' opponents have shot this season.


              TOP PERFORMERS: LaMelo Ball is scoring 18.6 points per game with 3.6 rebounds and 6.2 assists for the Timberwolves. Ayo Dosunmu is averaging 20.2 points and 4.5 rebounds while shooting 53.4% over the past 10 games.


              Deni Avdija is averaging 23.9 points, 6.1 rebounds and 6.3 assists for the Trail Blazers. Damian Lillard is averaging 2.9 made 3-pointers over the last 10 games.


              LAST 10 GAMES: Timberwolves: 6-4, averaging 117.5 points, 46.8 rebounds, 25.9 assists, 8.8 steals and 5.3 blocks per game while shooting 47.6% from the field. Their opponents have averaged 109.5 points per game.


              Trail Blazers: 7-3, averaging 118.3 points, 43.0 rebounds, 24.2 assists, 6.5 steals and 5.5 blocks per game while shooting 46.7% from the field. Their opponents have averaged 113.9 points.


              INJURIES: Timberwolves: Donte DiVincenzo: out (achilles), Jaylen Clark: day to day (hamstring), Anthony Edwards: out (knee).


              Trail Blazers: Chris Youngblood: day to day (foot), Shaedon Sharpe: out (meniscus), Vit Krejci: out (leg), Ja Morant: out (hamstring).


              ------


              The Associated Press created this story using technology provided by Data Skrive and data from Sportradar.
